name: Vals AI homepage: private benchmarks for legal, tax and finance
title: Vals AI homepage: private benchmarks for legal, tax and finance
answer: Vals AI is a publisher of private, domain-specific benchmarks in legal, tax and finance. Its homepage reports model evaluations on those benchmarks, including a Vals Index ranking and cost per test. The most useful point for accounting readers is that it reports measured scores and cost per test for models on finance and tax benchmarks, though the page itself is a collection of short evaluation updates rather than a detailed accounting study.

sections.body: Vals AI publishes this homepage, which describes private, domain-specific benchmarks in legal, tax and finance. The page is a collection of short evaluation notes and benchmark announcements, with model entries dated 2026/09/22. The source was harvested on 2026-09-26. It covers model results on the Vals Index and several named benchmarks, including Code Migration, Public Benefits Bench, SRE Bench, MedCode, Legal Research, VoiceCodeBench, CUA-bench and Vibe Code Bench 1-100. It is a company homepage rather than a full research paper or methodology document.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: Vals AI describes private, domain-specific benchmarks in legal, tax and finance. Its homepage is a running set of evaluation notes, with entries dated 2026/09/22. It reports results for OpenAI GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5, Xiaomi MiMo V2.6 Pro and MiMo V2.6 Flash, and other models. The Vals Index ranks models by reported performance and cost per test. GPT-6 Luna places 20th of 65 at 58.45% and $0.42 per test, the lowest cost in the top 20 and roughly 18 times cheaper than GPT-6 Sol at 62.57% and $7.56. MiMo V2.6 Flash places 16th of 65 at 59.58% and $0.20 per test, with MiMo V2.6 Pro 17th at 59.47% and $0.39 per test. Both are described as the top-scoring open-weight models on the Index. The page also reports a Claude Opus 5.5 agent experiment that produced a formally verified shortest-path improvement in Lean within 15 hours and 733 message-board posts. Other items cover voice transcription, a computer-use benchmark for video games, a web application benchmark, and model pricing and context windows. The finance and tax benchmarks are named in the opening line, but the homepage does not show the underlying tasks or scoring method.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: Vals AI states that GPT-6 Sol costs $2.00 per million input tokens and $10.00 per million output tokens, with long-context requests at $4.00 and $15.00, a 1M-token context window and 128k max output tokens. It states that GPT-6 Luna costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, with long-context requests at $0.20 and $0.75, a 1M-token context window and 128k max output tokens. The page says GPT-6 Luna places 20th of 65 on the Vals Index at 58.45% and $0.42 per test, the lowest cost in the top 20 and roughly 18 times cheaper than GPT-6 Sol at 62.57% and $7.56. It says MiMo V2.6 Flash places 16th of 65 at 59.58% and $0.20 per test, with MiMo V2.6 Pro 17th at 59.47% and $0.39 per test. It says both are the top-scoring open-weight models on the Index, ahead of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 57.86% and Kimi K3 at 57.81%, and within a point of Grok 4.7 at 60.22% and GPT-5.6 Luna at 59.88%. It says Claude Opus 5.5 costs $4.00 per million input tokens and $20.00 per million output tokens, with a 1M-token context window and 128k max output tokens. It says ten Claude Opus 5.5 agents produced C-HD in 15 hours and 733 message-board posts. It says Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0 has a 2.41s mean time-to-first-partial, on par with GPT Live Transcribe at 2.52s, and a 90.6% CTEM second to GPT Live Transcribe at 91.4%, with a 10.5% word error rate. It says CUA-bench gives each model one three-hour trial per game across six commercial video games, with three public games named as Minecraft, SUPERHOT and eFootball, and a held-out game of the same genre. It says GPT-6 Astra leads CUA-bench at 19.2%, ahead of Claude Fable 5.1 at 13.2%, Claude Opus 5 at 9.0%, GPT-5.6 Sol at 8.3% and Gemini 3.8 Flash at 4.2%, and no model clears a fifth of the suite. It says no model plays at human speed, with models acting once every 15 to 59 seconds and sending 2 to 19 inputs a minute. It says Hy4 Preview has a 1M-token context window and 64k max output tokens, priced at $0.83 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens, accessed through OpenRouter.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader tracking AI in accounting, this source is useful because it names tax and finance as benchmark areas and reports model scores and cost per test on the Vals Index. It can help compare models on reported accuracy and price for finance and tax work. It also shows that model choice involves trade-offs between score and cost, for example GPT-6 Luna at 58.45% and $0.42 per test against GPT-6 Sol at 62.57% and $7.56. The page does not provide accounting-specific benchmarks, so an accounting reader should treat it as a starting point for model evaluation rather than a complete accounting assessment.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Accounting

sections.body: This is a company homepage, not a full report. It gives short evaluation notes and selected results, with entries dated 2026/09/22 and a harvest date of 2026-09-26. It does not show the underlying tasks or scoring method for the benchmarks. It names legal, tax and finance as domains but does not give accounting-specific benchmarks or accounting task results. Much of the page covers non-finance topics such as video games, voice transcription and web application coding. The results are therefore partial and should be read as a snapshot of the publisher's own benchmark suite.
